subcategory: Integer overflow feeding an allocation size
title: Integer overflow leading to a heap overflow
root_cause: count * sizeof(item) is computed in 32-bit arithmetic. When the true product exceeds 2^32, it silently wraps to a small number, so malloc() allocates far less memory than the code then writes into.
defenses: Do size arithmetic in size_t (or wider), not a narrower integer type.
Check for overflow before allocating, e.g. with __builtin_mul_overflow or calloc(n, size).
Treat any size or count that comes from outside the program as hostile until range-checked.
Build with -fsanitize=undefined,integer in testing to catch wraparounds.
